sources.title: Michael S. Floater and Kai Hormann, Barycentric rational interpolation with no poles and high rates of approximation
sources.locator: Full 17-page author-hosted preprint; Sections 2–4; Theorem 1 and its denominator-sign proof; Theorem 2 for d≥1; Theorem 3 for d=0; barycentric weight formula (18).
sources.source_kind_detail: Author-hosted full-text preprint. This is the full paper specified by the owner correction, not the earlier one-page security-challenge response from the published-paper endpoint.
sources.not_read: The preprint was previously recorded as read in the APP-RATIONAL ROOT planning packet. In this dispatch the matching published paper's complete Theorem 1 and Theorems 2–3 arguments were also opened and inspected. The new bounded-variation extension and uniform-grid counterexample are proved locally; they are not attributed to this source.

contents.name: Floater–Hormann local-polynomial blend, positive denominator and no-real-pole proof
contents.support: The item reproduces the complete alternating-sign and decreasing-magnitude argument for all node gaps, nodes, and both exterior intervals.

contents.name: Barycentric weight identity and support interpolation
contents.support: The item expands every local Lagrange polynomial, interchanges the finite sums, and derives the exact weight formula.

contents.name: Theorem 2, d≥1 C^(d+2) parity bounds
contents.support: The item proves the divided-difference numerator estimate, the denominator lower bound, the even-m leftover term, and the exact constants.

contents.name: Theorem 3, d=0 C^2 parity bounds and local mesh ratio
contents.support: The item separately proves the endpoint and interior denominator estimates using the local mesh ratio beta.

contents.name: Comparison of the local beta with the global mesh ratio
contents.support: The item proves beta≤h/h_min directly from the largest and smallest adjacent gaps.

contents.name: Distinct-node divided differences and the Lagrange leading-coefficient formula
contents.support: The local definition fixes the recursive convention; the adjacent local lemma proves the Lagrange formula and symmetry used by the Floater–Hormann derivations.

contents.name: Repeated Rolle bound and adjacent-window recurrence
contents.support: The two local lemmas supply the derivative bound and the recurrence for adjacent divided-difference windows; their complete arguments are included.

contents.name: Hermite–Genocchi simplex representation
contents.support: The local lemma proves the simplex integral from the recursive divided-difference formula and Newton–Leibniz; the paper is source context, not a substitute for that proof.

contents.name: Hermite–Genocchi bounded-variation window estimate
contents.reason: This is a locally proved consequence of the simplex formula and the definition of total variation; the source is not cited as proving it.

contents.name: C^(d+1) bounded-variation extension
contents.reason: This rate is independently proved from the local simplex and variation lemmas; the source does not state or prove this extension.

contents.name: Uniform-grid counterexample to a seminorm-only rate
contents.reason: This complete counterexample is required by the owner correction and is proved locally; it is not attributed to the source.

read_evidence.access_method: Reused the actual complete preprint reading recorded in research/numerical-analysis-remaining-71-2026-10-17-ROOT-rational-planning-cycle1/report.md and proof.md; in this dispatch also opened the complete published PDF and inspected its theorem proofs at the listed locators.
read_evidence.extent: The complete full-text PDF was available. The full proof of Theorem 1 and the full proofs of Theorems 2 and 3 were inspected. No claim that citations alone establish the local items is made.

sources.title: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Olivier Sète, and Lloyd N. Trefethen, The AAA algorithm for rational approximation
sources.locator: Complete 29-page accepted manuscript; Sections 2–4, equations (2.1)–(2.5), (3.4)–(3.8), Proposition 3.1, and the exact-arithmetic MATLAB core algorithm in Section 4.
sources.source_kind_detail: Author-hosted full-text accepted manuscript of SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 40(3), A1494–A1522 (2018).
sources.not_read: The full paper was opened. The listed sections, propositions, and algorithm are the only portions used. Applications outside the core scalar finite-sample algorithm are not claimed as proof premises.

contents.name: Barycentric representation and support interpolation
contents.support: The item gives the cleared polynomial quotient, support values, and reduced-denominator pole convention.

contents.name: Nonzero cleared barycentric denominator
contents.support: The local argument evaluates the cleared denominator polynomial at any support node with nonzero weight.

contents.name: Greedy support selection and Loewner least-squares matrix
contents.support: The item follows the exact finite-sample Loewner/SVD core with explicit deterministic tie, zero-weight, pole, tolerance, and budget branches.

contents.name: Minimum singular-vector residual and support interpolation
contents.support: The item proves the singular-vector minimization locally and states that it is a linearized Loewner residual, not a uniform or nonlinear minimax guarantee.

contents.name: Rational transfer-function pole example
contents.support: The finite run and the pole at z=2 are verified by exact algebra in the example.

contents.name: Small sampled residual without an off-grid guarantee
contents.support: The finite zero-data run and arbitrary off-grid discrepancy are verified directly.

read_evidence.access_method: Opened the full author-hosted PDF through the web reader and inspected the complete barycentric representation, Loewner least-squares derivation, Proposition 3.1, pole discussion, and algorithm code.
read_evidence.extent: The complete 29-page manuscript was accessible. The supported argument uses Sections 2–4; the paper's applications are not treated as guarantees for this batch.

sources.title: Jean-Paul Berrut and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation
sources.locator: Complete 17-page SIAM Review paper; Sections 2–4 and Section 9.2, Rational Interpolation, printed pp. 501–517.
sources.source_kind_detail: Author-hosted full-text copy of SIAM Review 46(3), 501–517 (2004), DOI 10.1137/S0036144502417715.
sources.not_read: The complete paper was opened; Sections 2–4 and 9.2 are the relevant independent treatment. Numerical stability estimates elsewhere in the paper are outside the claims made here.

contents.name: Nonzero cleared barycentric denominator
contents.support: Section 9.2 gives the arbitrary-weight rational barycentric representation; the batch proves the denominator polynomial is nonzero by evaluation at a support node.

contents.name: Lagrange and Newton interpolation bases
contents.support: The local proposition proves the rational quotient directly; this paper independently records the polynomial barycentric identity and its support convention.

contents.name: Rational interpolation with arbitrary nonzero barycentric weights
contents.support: Section 9.2 confirms the arbitrary-weight quotient is a rational interpolant and discusses poles and attainable points.

contents.name: Polynomial and rational barycentric formula conventions
contents.support: The source provides an independent treatment of the numerator/denominator form; the FH-specific weight expansion is proved locally.

contents.name: Distinct-node divided differences and Lagrange formula
contents.support: The local proof establishes the leading-coefficient formula and its symmetry for the distinct real-node convention used here.

read_evidence.access_method: Opened the complete author-hosted PDF and inspected the Lagrange cardinal formulas and Section 9.2 rational-interpolation discussion.
read_evidence.extent: All 17 PDF pages were accessible. Only the named mathematical sections are claimed as relevant.
